stories.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto Flu’: is the whole world really taking the day off work to play GTA VI?
summary: Headlines have claimed the release of the first new GTA game in 13 years will hugely affect the global economy on Thursday – but there’s another story that’s been left behindA new pandemic is threatening planet Earth.

It should pass in a few days.The anticipation for Grand Theft Auto VI, the first new game in the franchise in 13 years, is so high that a steady stream of news coverage has suggested it heralds economic catastrophe due to workers taking time off to play the game.
The term “GTA Flu” was coined for the swathe of sickies that reportedly happened when GTA V was released in 2013, and – supposedly – are set to happen again when GTA VI comes out this week.

stories.title: Ten years, thousands of staff and a billion dollars: the exclusive inside story of Grand Theft Auto VI
summary: As a student in Edinburgh at that time, I would hear rumours of wild parties at the executives’ houses, as decadent as those in the game.

Grand Theft Auto is now made by a huge team of nearly 5,000 people around the world but its central nervous system is still in Holyrood, in the shadow of Arthur’s Seat.The setting of the latest Grand Theft Auto game really could not be further from the Scottish capital.
Grand Theft Auto VI takes us to Vice City in the state of Leonida, a parody of Miami, Florida.
